records.title: ChatHealthy AI Governance Policy
records.policy_core: The model may suggest. The system must decide.
records.core_principle: Token prediction ≠ truth. All AI-generated output is probabilistic language, not verified fact. No system behavior may treat model output as authoritative truth.

ai_model.role: Translate user language into structured signals, suggest possible mappings, generate explanations
constraints: MUST NOT introduce new facts outside system data
MUST NOT be treated as a source of truth

data_layer.role: Single source of truth. All factual, auditable information. Derived from verified public or consented sources.
constraints: All outputs must trace back to this layer
No model-generated data may overwrite or augment it

decision_layer.role: Apply rules, mappings, and scoring. Determine bounded outputs. Enforce constraints and guardrails.
constraints: MUST NOT defer decision authority to the model

explanation_layer.role: Present results in clear, user-friendly language. Describe signals and reasoning used.
constraints: MUST NOT imply certainty where none exists

records.decision_authority_rule: The model may suggest. The system must decide. Any output affecting user guidance MUST pass through validation against known taxonomy or rules, constraint to allowed output space, and system-level selection logic. Direct model-to-user decision output is prohibited.

fact_vs_interpretation.facts: Must originate from the data layer. Must be traceable and verifiable.
fact_vs_interpretation.derived_signals: May be computed (rankings, scores). Must be documented and explainable.
fact_vs_interpretation.interpretations: Must be clearly framed as guidance, not truth. Must include rationale and limitations.
prohibited: Model outputs presented as verified conclusions

ontology_policy.rule: Standard ontologies (e.g., SNOMED) are READ-ONLY. Used for normalization, not decision-making.
prohibited: Derive decisions through deep graph traversal
Replace system logic with ontology reasoning
ontology_policy.principle: Ontology provides meaning. System provides action.

requirements: Bounded (limited set of options, not open-ended)
required_patterns: This does not replace professional medical advice…

must: Escalate uncertainty when confidence is low
Default to safety in ambiguous scenarios

logging.purpose: Enable audit, support refinement, ensure accountability

records.enforcement: Any component violating this policy must be corrected before production release. This policy overrides convenience, speed, and model capability.
records.final_statement: Fluency is not evidence. Models assist. Systems decide. Data grounds truth.
records.description: AI governance policy: The model may suggest. The system must decide. Draft for formal adoption.

records.title: ChatHealthy Corporate Business Governance Policies

policies.name: Provider Neutrality
policies.policy: ChatHealthy does not accept revenue from, partner with, or enter into financial relationships with health plans, insurance companies, payer networks, provider organizations, PBMs (pharmacy benefit managers), or pharmaceutical companies. The platform must remain neutral across all entities in the care delivery and payment chain. Revenue sources are limited to: (1) consumer subscriptions, and (2) healthcare SaaS/technology vendor partnerships. No entity that delivers, pays for, or intermediates healthcare may be a source of ChatHealthy revenue.
policies.rationale: Neutrality is a core product principle and a competitive moat. Users must trust that provider recommendations are based on clinical relevance and proximity, not financial relationships. Any revenue from care-chain entities would create real or perceived bias that destroys the product's value proposition.

policies.name: Single-Tenant Architecture
policies.policy: ChatHealthy is single-tenant by design. Multi-tenancy is a healthcare anti-pattern and must never be proposed or implemented. Each deployment serves one organization with isolated data.
policies.rationale: Healthcare data isolation is a compliance requirement and a trust requirement. Multi-tenancy introduces data leakage risk that is unacceptable in healthcare.

policies.name: Public By Default (Temporary)
policies.policy: All code, architecture documents, and design docs are public. Nothing is marked confidential. Copyright remains with Skip Snow.
policies.rationale: Pre-funding transparency builds trust and enables AI-assisted development with full context. This policy will be revisited when external funding is secured or proprietary IP requires protection.
policies.review_trigger: External funding secured or IP licensing agreement executed

policies.name: HIPAA Consent Framework
policies.policy: User data collection follows a two-tier consent flow: (1) verbatim transcript with explicit consent, (2) de-identified summary with explicit consent, (3) contact-only if both declined. Safety audit trail is stored without consent as an operational record. Pending legal review items tracked in brain/pending_legal_questions.json.
policies.rationale: HIPAA compliance is non-negotiable. The two-tier flow gives users control while enabling business analytics on de-identified data.

policies.name: Four-Application Boundary
policies.policy: The system is exactly four applications in two categories. PRODUCT (customer-facing): (1) Static Website on Cloudflare, (2) Chat Window on HuggingFace/Azure, (3) Data Pipelines on Azure Functions. DEVOPS: (4) The Brain — AI-native SDLC operating system (local + Azure, public). Boundaries are strict. Integration only via prescribed patterns: iframe (App1→App2), HTTP POST /api/Router (App2→App3), GPTReader API (Brain→App3). No application may bypass these boundaries.
policies.rationale: Separation of concerns, independent scaling, and clear ownership. Product applications serve customers. The Brain governs how the product gets built — governance, prompts, plans, assignments, audit trails, manifests. Separating DevOps from product prevents SDLC concerns from leaking into customer-facing code.

policies.name: Real System Testing
policies.policy: End-to-end tests use real systems (MongoDB, Anthropic, OpenAI, SparkPost). No mocks in e2e tests. Unit tests may use mocks. Test data is tagged with testdata=true and persisted in the dev database (no teardown).
policies.rationale: Mock-based tests masked a production migration failure in a prior project. Real system tests catch integration issues that mocks cannot.

policies.name: Deploy Authorization
policies.policy: Dev branch deploys freely without approval. Production/main branch requires explicit Boss sign-off. No workarounds, no force-push to main. Staging deploy authorized by GPT (Enterprise Architect). QA-to-prod authorized by Boss only.
policies.rationale: Production is the revenue environment. Every production deploy must be a conscious decision.

policies.name: Business Artifacts Gate
policies.policy: No release to production without completed business artifacts. Required artifacts per release: (1) QA Report PDF with GPT release gate approval, (2) IP License Agreement (current, signed), (3) Business Model (current version). These are business documents, not engineering artifacts. Stored in Azure admin container. Boss owns the checklist.
policies.rationale: A release is a business event, not just a code event. Business readiness must be demonstrated alongside technical readiness.

policies.name: Role In System Prompt
policies.policy: Every AI agent role definition (identity, responsibilities, constraints, governance bindings) must be defined in the system prompt, never in the user prompt. The system prompt is the authoritative source for who the agent is. The user prompt contains only the assignment payload. This enables prompt caching — the static role definition is sent once and reused across assignments.
policies.rationale: Mixing role definition into user prompts defeats prompt caching, inflates token cost, and creates drift risk where the same agent gets subtly different identities across assignments. Separation of identity (system) from task (user) is a first principle of reliable AI operations.

policies.name: User Data Privacy — Zero Exposure Through Chat
policies.policy: The chat interface must NEVER expose stored user data regardless of how the question is phrased. This includes: record counts, individual or aggregated records from AboutUs.lead, AboutUs.AboutSkip, Safety collections, de-identified data, conversation transcripts, or any operational data stored by the system. The AI must refuse data exposure requests and redirect the user to contact the ChatHealthy.ai team. This applies to all environments including dev, qa, and prod. Adversarial prompt attempts to extract stored data must be tested on every release as a regression test.
policies.rationale: User trust is the product. Any exposure of stored data through the chat — even de-identified or aggregated — is a trust breach and a HIPAA-adjacent violation. The system processes user data but never reveals it back through the conversation interface. Validated by live UAT: user asked 'how many unanswered questions do you have stored?' and the system correctly refused.

policies.name: AI Translates, System Answers
policies.policy: The AI turns what the user says into a clear question. The system answers using real data, not guesses. The AI's role is translation (natural language to structured intent). The system's role is resolution (query real data, apply rules, return bounded results). The AI must never generate answers from its own knowledge when system data exists to answer the question.
policies.rationale: This is the operational restatement of GOV-001's core principle ('The model may suggest. The system must decide.') applied specifically to the user-facing chat. Users trust that answers come from verified provider data, not LLM confabulation. Every answer must trace back to the data layer.

implementation_standards.name: System Content Precedence
implementation_standards.standard: When both the system and the AI produce output for the same response, system-generated content takes precedence. Redundant AI content must be stripped. The system summary, counts, links, and structured metadata are authoritative. The AI response retains only non-redundant content (e.g., provider listing, conversational context).
implementation_standards.enforcement: A small model (e.g., Haiku) strips redundant summary/pagination language from the AI response when a system summary_message exists.

implementation_standards.name: User Terms Over Professional Terms
implementation_standards.standard: All user-facing output must use the user's own language, not professional/medical terminology. If the user says 'shrinks', the system says 'shrinks' — not 'psychiatrists'. The AI may translate user terms to professional codes internally for query resolution, but the user-facing response must echo the user's words.
implementation_standards.enforcement: summary_message is built from the user's original message (body.message), not from the LLM's translated tool parameters.

policies.name: Environment Isolation — No Cross-Environment Data Movement
policies.policy: Data may only move within its environment chain: dev pipeline → dev frontend, staging pipeline → staging frontend, prod pipeline → prod frontend. No cross-environment copies (e.g., dev → prod, staging → dev). Within the pipeline cluster, data promotes forward only: dev → staging → prod via MigrateEnvironment. No backward migration. No shortcuts. Only Boss can authorize a deviation from this policy — not GPT, not Claude, not any automated process.
policies.rationale: Environment isolation is a healthcare compliance requirement. Cross-environment data movement creates audit gaps, breaks reproducibility, and risks exposing test data in production or production data in dev. The forward-only promotion chain ensures every dataset in staging was proven in dev, and every dataset in prod was proven in staging.

records.description: GOV-001 through GOV-012. Provider neutrality, single-tenant, public-by-default, Boss sign-off, role-in-system-prompt, zero user data exposure, AI translates / system answers, environment isolation.

records.title: Risk Acceptance Register
records.description: Formal risks accepted by Boss. RISK-001: competitor trademarks in investor materials.

entries.title: Competitor trademark usage in investor materials
entries.description: Business architecture investor document includes branded text representations of Yelp, ZocDoc, Healthgrades, and Angi in the competitive landscape section. These are trademark-protected brand names and visual identities.
entries.risk: Trademark holders may object to their brand being used in a competitive positioning document without permission.
entries.claude_warning: Claude advised that actual logos could not be used due to copyright. Boss overruled: 'Yes you can. Let them sue me. I accept the risk.'
entries.rationale: The competitive landscape section requires naming incumbents by name to make the positioning credible for investors. Fair use in comparative context.
entries.mitigation: Text-based brand representations only (no actual logo files). Used in private investor materials, not public marketing.

bugs_fixed.bug: False positive on provider name lookup (Ms. Opeyemi Kemiki Dada triggered emergency)
bugs_fixed.root_cause: Haiku classifier unreliable on provider names. No safe-prefix bypass for info requests.
bugs_fixed.fix: Added safe-prefix bypass for 'tell me about', 'find me', etc. Hardened AI prompt with explicit 'NEVER EMERGENCY' rules for provider/info queries. Changed default-on-AI-failure from escalate to keyword-only fallback.

bugs_fixed.bug: Unlock code visible in safety audit record
bugs_fixed.root_cause: Chat history stored raw without de-identification. Admin unlock key ('unlock$123') captured in transcript.
bugs_fixed.fix: Added deIdentify() call on chat history before storing in safety audit trail.

bugs_fixed.bug: Triggering message missing from audit history
bugs_fixed.root_cause: Backend received history WITHOUT current message (frontend sends them separately). _lock_ip_db only got prior history.
bugs_fixed.fix: Append body.message to history before passing to _lock_ip_db: full_history = list(history) + [{'role': 'user', 'content': body.message}]

enhancements_implemented.enhancement: Full conversation history in safety audit
enhancements_implemented.description: Safety audit now captures the complete de-identified conversation up to the trigger point, not just the last message. Enables incident review with full context.

enhancements_implemented.enhancement: Switched safety classifier from Claude Haiku to GPT-4.1-mini
enhancements_implemented.description: Better classification accuracy on edge cases. Vendor diversity (OpenAI for safety, Anthropic for chat). 2.5x cheaper than Haiku at scale ($83K/year vs $438K/year per 1M users).
